learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the magic of reproduction! Discover how artists create multiple copies of an artwork using blocks, stamps, and stencils.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Printmaking is the process of creating artworks by printing on paper. Unlike drawing or painting, it allows the artist to produce multiple original copies (called an edition) from a single master plate or block.

In relief printing, you carve away the parts you don't want to print. The raised surface is inked and pressed onto paper. Vegetable prints (like using a cut potato or ladyfinger) are simple examples of relief printing.
A stencil is a piece of paper, plastic, or metal with a design cut out of it. Paint or ink is applied over the stencil, passing through the holes to create the image on the surface below.
Unlike other printmaking methods, mono-printing creates a single, unique print. Ink is painted onto a smooth surface (like glass) and then transferred to paper before it dries.
Advanced relief techniques where designs are carved into linoleum sheets (linocut) or blocks of wood (woodcut) using special carving tools.

fun_activity.title: 🥔 The Potato Stamp
fun_activity.instructions: Take a large potato and cut it in half. Ask an adult to help you carve a simple shape (like a star or heart) into the flat side, cutting away the background. Dip the raised star into poster color and stamp it on paper to create a wrapping paper pattern!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly differentiate between Relief printing (ink is on the raised surface) and Stencil printing (ink passes through cut-out holes).
📌 Woodcut is one of the oldest and most traditional forms of relief printmaking.
📌 Remember that each copy in a printmaking series is called an 'impression'.
quick_recap: ⭐ Printmaking allows an artist to create an 'edition' of multiple identical artworks.
⭐ Stencils are highly popular in street art (like Banksy's work) because they allow for quick and precise painting.
⭐ Always apply ink evenly using a roller (brayer) for the best relief print.
